facts.text: ISO 19014 is the family of standards for designing, building, testing and programming earth-moving machine electronic safety-related control systems so that faults do not cause harm, including systems behind automatic braking.
facts.quote: ISO 19014 is the family of standards that tells a maker of earth-moving machines

facts.text: ISO provides ISO 13849 as a generic machinery functional-safety method, while road vehicles have ISO 26262; the booklet identifies ISO 19014, not ISO 26262, as the appropriate framework for earth-moving machines.
facts.quote: For earth-moving machines the sector framework is ISO 19014, and the booklet is clear that this, not ISO 26262, is the right one [Chapter 3].

facts.text: ISO 19014 uses Machine Performance Level (MPL): hazard and risk analysis assigns each safety function a required level, MPLr, and design evaluation must show an achieved level, MPLa, at least as high. Machine Control System Safety Analysis (MCSSA) is the method for assigning MPLr.
facts.quote: A hazard and risk analysis assigns a required level, MPLr, to each safety function; the design is then evaluated to show an achieved level, MPLa, at least as high. The method for MPLr is the Machine Control System Safety Analysis (MCSSA) [Chapter 3].

facts.text: ISO 19014-1 provides the MCSSA method and MPLr.
facts.quote: Part 1 gives the MCSSA method and MPLr

facts.text: ISO 19014-2 covers hardware, architecture and achieved Machine Performance Level (MPLa).
facts.quote: Part 2 covers hardware, architecture and MPLa

facts.text: ISO 19014-3 sets vibration, temperature and electrical-robustness environmental tests for safety-related electronics.
facts.quote: Part 3 sets environmental tests (vibration, temperature, electrical robustness) for the safety-related electronics

facts.text: ISO 19014-4 covers software and data transmission.
facts.quote: Part 4 covers software and data transmission

facts.text: ISO 19014-5 provides MPLr tables for common functions that manufacturers can use without a full MCSSA for each new model, provided the tables' assumptions hold.
facts.quote: Part 5 gives tables of MPLr for common functions so a manufacturer can apply them "without performing a full MCSSA for each new model" when the tables' assumptions hold [Chapter 3].

facts.text: ISO 19014-2 covers systems controlling machine motion or mitigating a hazard and excludes awareness systems that do not affect motion, such as cameras and radar detectors. A warning-only system is outside its scope, whereas a system able to command brakes is inside.
facts.quote: ISO 19014-2 covers systems that control machine motion or mitigate a hazard and excludes "awareness systems that do not impact machine motion (e.g. cameras and radar detectors)". A warning-only system is outside; a system that can command the brakes is inside

facts.text: The booklet recommends separately analyzing failure to intervene when needed and intervention when unsafe or unnecessary as two safety functions.
facts.quote: The booklet asks for two safety functions to be analyzed separately: failure to intervene when needed, and intervention when it is unsafe or unnecessary

facts.text: An unexpected full brake application on a loaded truck on a slope is itself a hazard.
facts.quote: an unexpected full brake on a loaded truck on a slope is itself a hazard [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Edition 2 of ISO 19014 Parts 1–4 and the first full-standard edition of Part 5, replacing ISO/TS 19014-5:2021, reached “under publication” in August 2026 and were scheduled for October 2026.
facts.quote: edition 2 of Parts 1 to 4 and the first full-standard edition of Part 5 (replacing ISO/TS 19014-5:2021) reached "under publication" in August 2026, scheduled for October 2026

facts.text: European adoption of ISO 19014-1 was in approval at CEN alongside the 2026 ISO 19014 series changes.
facts.quote: with a European adoption of Part 1 in approval at the European standards body CEN [Chapter 3].

facts.text: ISO 19014 replaced ISO 15998, which was withdrawn in June 2022.
facts.quote: ISO 19014 replaced ISO 15998, withdrawn in June 2022.

facts.text: Whether ISO 19014-5 tables contain a collision-avoidance entry was not reviewed, and no published MPLr for collision avoidance was found.
facts.quote: Whether the Part 5 tables contain an entry for collision avoidance was not reviewed; no published MPLr for this function was found [Chapter 3].

facts.text: No simulation wording was found in the ISO 19014 review reported in Chapter 12.
facts.quote: No simulation wording was found [Chapter 12]

facts.text: The booklet treats simulation as admissible functional-safety design evidence because functional safety inherently rests on analytical evidence, even where no standard accepts simulation as a replacement for physical testing.
facts.quote: functional safety does rest on analytical evidence by nature, which is why the booklet treats simulation as admissible design evidence even where no standard accepts it as a replacement for a physical test [Chapter 3].

facts.text: ISO 19014-4 excludes cybersecurity.
facts.quote: Part 4 excludes cybersecurity

facts.text: Whether ISO 19014-4 requires tool qualification was not found.
facts.quote: whether it requires tool qualification was not found

facts.text: ISO 19014-3 environmental tests do not establish camera, lidar or radar perception-chain performance across visibility and weather combinations.
facts.quote: Part 3's environmental tests are "not the same as proving a camera, lidar or radar perception chain across visibility and weather combinations" [Chapters 3, 12, 13].

facts.text: Adding a brake command brings the product into ISO 19014 scope, so the program plan needs MPLr assignment, architecture and fault evidence, environmental qualification and software-process evidence against editions expected in October 2026.
facts.quote: the plan needs an MPLr assignment, architecture and fault evidence, environmental qualification and software process evidence, all against editions that appear in October 2026 [Chapter 3].

facts.text: The booklet identifies ISO 19014-5 tables as the only sourced route to reducing per-model analysis burden when many machine models must be covered in four months.
facts.quote: The Part 5 tables are the only sourced route to reducing the per-model analysis burden when many machine models must be covered in four months [Chapter 3].
